NDT training in Aiken: how it works for Aiken employers and technicians

Short answer: Atlantis NDT delivers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training for employers and technicians in Aiken and the Central Savannah River Area. Theory runs live online, and practical training runs onsite at your facility. Level I, II and III courses cover UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET under ASNT Level III oversight. Your employer certifies you under its written practice, and nuclear-sector employers may add site-specific qualification on top.

That last point is what sets Aiken apart. In most US cities, SNT-TC-1A training, documented experience and employer certification are the whole story. Around the Savannah River Site and the commercial nuclear plant across the river in Georgia, an NDT technician's qualification usually sits inside a larger nuclear quality-assurance framework. The employer's QA programme decides which procedures are approved, how personnel qualification is documented and audited, and which additional site training, access requirements or performance demonstrations apply. Method training is still the foundation, but it is one layer of several.

We are careful about what we claim. Atlantis has no training centre in Aiken, Augusta or North Augusta. We deliver theory live online and practicals onsite at the employer's facility under ASNT Level III oversight. We do not provide DOE site-specific qualification, security clearances or commercial-nuclear performance demonstration. We do provide rigorous SNT-TC-1A method training, and we can help contractors in the region write and maintain the written practices that their nuclear customers will audit.

If you already know what you need, request an Aiken training quote. Cohort and onsite quotes are returned within one business day.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Aiken

All courses are built on ASNT SNT-TC-1A. Recommended training and experience hours by method and level are listed in our training-requirements matrix. Nuclear-sector written practices often require more than those minimums, so always check your employer's document.

MethodLevelsWhat Aiken-area employers use it forPrerequisite
UT (ultrasonic)I, II, III prepThickness and weld examination on process piping, tanks and vessels at nuclear-materials and waste-processing facilities; fabrication inspection for nuclear-quality components; power-plant pipingNone for Level I; Level I plus documented experience for Level II
PAUT (phased array)II, III prepEncoded weld examination and corrosion mapping where owners require full recorded data; new-construction piping and vessel weldsUT Level II or UT knowledge accepted by the written practice
TOFDII, III prepHeavy-section weld sizing on vessels and thick piping, usually with PAUTUT Level II
RT (radiographic)I, II, III prepNew-construction and repair welds on piping and vessels to ASME code; fabrication-shop radiography; interpretation of film and digital imagesNone for Level I; radiographer certification and radiation-safety requirements are separate
MT (magnetic particle)I, II, III prepCarbon-steel structures, supports, rotating equipment, and welds in industrial and power facilitiesNone for Level I
PT (liquid penetrant)I, II, III prepStainless-steel piping, tanks and components, which are widespread in nuclear-materials and waste-processing systems; weld root and final-surface checksNone for Level I
VT (visual)I, II, III prepWeld visual during fabrication and installation, in-service visual examination of structures and components, remote visual where access is restrictedNone for Level I
ET (eddy current)I, II, III prepHeat-exchanger and condenser tubing at power and industrial plants, surface crack detection on non-ferrous and austenitic componentsNone for Level I

UT. The course covers ultrasonic physics, calibration, straight-beam and angle-beam techniques, and DAC and TCG. It gives extra attention to the problems of austenitic stainless welds, where coarse grain structure scatters and skews the beam, because stainless steel is everywhere in the Aiken-area nuclear and chemical systems. Level II adds interpretation and reporting against ASME acceptance criteria.

PAUT and TOFD. These advanced courses cover focal laws, encoded scanning, data analysis and TOFD sizing. Nuclear owners often want a full recorded data set so it can be reviewed and archived, which makes encoded ultrasonics especially relevant here.

RT. The course covers radiation sources, exposure technique, image quality indicators, film and digital detectors, and weld interpretation to ASME Section V and the construction code. Radiation-safety licensing and radiographer certification are separate legal requirements, covered below.

MT and PT. PT is essential in this market because so many systems are stainless. The course covers penetrant families, removal methods, dwell and development, contaminant control (the chemistry of penetrant materials used on nuclear-grade stainless is often restricted, and procedures specify limits on sulphur and halogens), and interpretation. MT covers magnetisation techniques, particle selection and demagnetisation for the carbon-steel scope.

VT. Visual examination in nuclear work is formal and heavily documented. The course covers direct and remote visual, lighting and acuity verification, measurement, and the record-keeping that nuclear QA auditors expect.

ET. The course covers impedance-plane analysis, frequency and probe selection, and tube-inspection applications for the region's power plants and industrial heat exchangers.

Level III. Experienced technicians moving toward procedure ownership can prepare through our ASNT Level III programme. The exams themselves are administered by ASNT.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Aiken, step by step

  1. Establish the governing written practice. Your employer's written practice, together with any customer or site QA requirements that flow down to it, sets the rules. In nuclear work, ask early whether your customer's programme adds anything to the SNT-TC-1A baseline.
  2. Complete formal training. Classroom hours for the method and level, live online or onsite. Compare the training-requirements matrix with your written practice.
  3. Accumulate documented experience. Supervised experience in the method, logged and verified. Nuclear auditors check these records closely, so they need to be complete and traceable from the start.
  4. General exam. Written exam on the principles of the method, given under a Level III.
  5. Specific exam. Written exam on the employer's procedures, equipment, and the codes and specifications in use.
  6. Practical exam. Hands-on exam on specimens containing real discontinuities, graded by a Level III against the written practice.
  7. Vision exam. Near-vision acuity and colour-contrast testing. Near vision is re-checked at least annually.
  8. Employer certification. Written certification by the employer, with a complete, auditable file.
  9. Additional site requirements. Where applicable, the customer or site adds its own training, access and qualification steps. These are outside SNT-TC-1A and outside what Atlantis provides.
  10. Recertification. Follows the interval in your written practice (SNT-TC-1A recommends no more than five years), with lapse provisions for interrupted service.

More detail: SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Aiken crews

  • Live online theory. Instructor-led virtual sessions for the classroom hours. This suits shift workers and technicians across Aiken, Barnwell, Augusta and North Augusta. See online NDT training.
  • Onsite at your facility. Practical training and exams at your shop or facility, on your instruments and specimens. For contractors whose technicians work to specific approved procedures, this keeps the practical tied to the procedure they will actually use. Onsite delivery happens only where the host arranges access. Atlantis does not need, and does not claim, access to any secured government site.
  • Blended. Online theory followed by an onsite practical block.

Scheduling in the region follows outage and project calendars. Refuelling outages at commercial nuclear plants bring intense, planned periods of inspection demand, and project milestones on the DOE side create peaks of their own. Pulp, paper and chemical plants in the Augusta area take their own shutdowns. We schedule training before or between these windows, and theory can run in evening sessions. For programmes covering several methods or sites, see corporate NDT training.

The practical exam is always hands-on. Ask about onsite training for your Aiken crew.

Where NDT technicians work in Aiken

The Savannah River Site and its contractors. The DOE site south of Aiken handles nuclear-materials processing, tritium operations, liquid-waste treatment and vitrification, environmental cleanup and large new-construction projects, and it hosts a national laboratory. NDT work comes through the site's prime contractors and a wide network of subcontractors and fabricators. DOE nuclear facilities work under a nuclear quality-assurance rule (10 CFR 830, Subpart A) and DOE's QA order. Contractors commonly carry these out using the consensus standard ASME NQA-1. Piping is typically designed and examined to ASME B31.3, and some components are built to ASME Section III or Section VIII. The practical result for technicians is that controlled procedures, qualified personnel and traceable records are enforced to a strictness that commercial industry rarely matches.

Commercial nuclear power across the river. The four-unit nuclear station near Waynesboro, Georgia, runs refuelling outages that need large in-service inspection crews. Commercial nuclear ISI is governed by ASME Section XI, which calls for NDE personnel qualified to ANSI/ASNT CP-189 rather than SNT-TC-1A. Certain UT examinations also require performance demonstration under Section XI Appendix VIII, administered through the industry's Performance Demonstration Initiative. We say this plainly: SNT-TC-1A training is good method grounding, but a technician aiming at commercial nuclear ISI will need the plant's or vendor's CP-189 qualification and any required performance demonstration on top.

Fabrication and nuclear-quality suppliers. Shops in the region fabricate piping, tanks, vessels and structural components, some to nuclear quality requirements. They are the most natural users of SNT-TC-1A-based programmes and written practices, and their NDT records are audited by the customers they supply.

Augusta-area industry. Across the river, Augusta and Richmond and Columbia counties have pulp and paper mills, chemical plants, and power and manufacturing facilities that use UT thickness, PT, MT, VT and ET during operation and shutdowns. Aiken County also has substantial manufacturing, including tyre and automotive-supplier plants and industrial parks, where fabrication and maintenance NDT is needed.

Radiography licensing: South Carolina and Georgia. Both states are NRC Agreement States. In South Carolina, radioactive materials used in industrial radiography are licensed by the South Carolina Department of Environmental Services (SCDES), which took over the programme from the former DHEC. Georgia runs its own Agreement State radioactive-materials programme. Because many Aiken-area crews work on both sides of the Savannah River, radiography companies must hold the right licence or reciprocity in each state they work in. Radiographers must hold radiographer certification (typically through the ASNT Industrial Radiography Radiation Safety Personnel programme or a recognised state programme) and work under the licensee's radiation-safety programme. On federal DOE sites, radiological work also falls under DOE's own radiation-protection rules. SNT-TC-1A RT certification covers technique and interpretation. It does not authorise the use of sources.

What Aiken-area employers ask for. Common requirements are SNT-TC-1A Level II in UT, PT, VT and MT; RT and radiographer certification for construction; and PAUT or TOFD for advanced roles. Many roles add nuclear QA experience, site-specific qualification and, for DOE work, the ability to obtain a security clearance. Commercial nuclear roles ask for CP-189 and performance-demonstration qualifications. Some postings also list CWI or ISO 9712. Those are separate schemes that Atlantis does not train. For pay by level, see our NDT salary guide.

Level III services and written practices for Aiken NDT companies

For a small or mid-sized contractor or fabricator supplying the nuclear market, the written practice and the certification files are what gets audited, often more closely than the inspection results themselves. Atlantis supports these companies with the following:

  • Written-practice development and revision. A written practice aligned with current SNT-TC-1A and structured so customer QA requirements can be layered on cleanly. See NDT written practice development.
  • Outsourced Level III. Exam preparation and administration, procedure and technique approval, and certification-file review.
  • Pre-audit record checks. We compare training, experience, exam and vision records against your written practice before a customer audit and help you close any gaps.
  • SNT-TC-1A guidance. SNT-TC-1A certification explains the employer-based model and how it relates to CP-189.

Book a Level III consultation and tell us your methods, headcount and the customer QA requirements you need to satisfy.

Practise before the practical exam

The Practical NDT 3D simulator offers 12 methods in 5 environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. Aiken-area trainees can use the lab, workshop and tank scenarios to rehearse calibration sequences, scan coverage and indication recognition between sessions.

It is a practice aid only. It does not replace hands-on training on real instruments or the practical exam on real specimens that your written practice requires, and it has no role in nuclear performance demonstration.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. As Level III he oversees course content, exams and practical assessments, and onsite programmes run under that oversight.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Aiken

How do I get NDT certified in Aiken?

Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, your employer certifies you after formal training, documented experience, general, specific and practical exams under a Level III, and a vision test. In nuclear work, the customer's QA programme or site may add further qualification steps. Atlantis provides the method training and written-practice support.

Can I take NDT training online in South Carolina?

Yes, for theory. Live online sessions cover the classroom hours. Practical training and exams must be hands-on, onsite at your employer's facility or in a scheduled practical block. See online NDT training.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

It depends on your employer's written practice and your starting point. SNT-TC-1A recommends minimum training and experience hours, which are listed in our training-requirements matrix. Nuclear-sector written practices may require more.

Do I need a license for radiography in South Carolina?

South Carolina is an Agreement State, so radioactive materials used in radiography are licensed by the South Carolina Department of Environmental Services. Georgia runs its own programme for work across the river. Radiographers must hold radiographer certification and work under the licensee's radiation-safety programme. SNT-TC-1A RT certification is a separate requirement.

What does NDT training cost in Aiken?

We do not publish prices. The cost depends on method, level, group size and whether delivery is online, onsite or blended. We return cohort and onsite quotes within one business day. Request an Aiken training quote.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Aiken employers?

Yes. SNT-TC-1A is widely used by contractors, fabricators and industrial employers in the region. Commercial nuclear in-service inspection uses ASNT's CP-189 standard, and DOE-site work adds site-specific requirements, so check what your target employer expects.

What is the difference between SNT-TC-1A and CP-189?

SNT-TC-1A is a recommended practice that employers adapt into their written practice. CP-189 is a stricter ASNT standard with mandatory requirements, and ASME Section XI calls for it in commercial nuclear in-service inspection. Atlantis trains to SNT-TC-1A.

Can Atlantis get me a DOE security clearance or site qualification?

No. Clearances are sponsored by the employer and granted by the government, and site-specific qualifications are run by the site's contractors. We provide the NDT method training that comes before those steps.

Why is PT so common in Aiken-area work?

Nuclear-materials, waste-processing and chemical systems use a lot of austenitic stainless steel, which MT cannot examine. PT is the main surface method there, often with controlled-chemistry penetrant materials.

Can you train our crew onsite?

Yes, at your own facility. Ask about onsite training for your Aiken crew.

We are a small supplier with no Level III. Can you help?

Yes. Outsourced Level III services include written-practice development, exam administration and record review. See written practice development.

How should I prepare for a Level II exam?

Study the theory, use mock exams such as our UT Level 2 practice questions, and rehearse on the Practical NDT simulator before the hands-on practical.
